case_name: Arvind Sharma & Others vs State Of Himachal Pradesh & Another

parties.respondent_defendant: State of Himachal Pradesh & another (wife's side)

facts_of_case: Matrimonial discord; FIR No. 160 of 2023 registered under Sections 498A, 504, 506 and 34 IPC; Private Complaint No. 5 of 2024 filed by respondent No. 2-Smt. Pooja Sharma

legal_principles.principle: The High Court has inherent power under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure to secure the ends of justice or to prevent abuse of process of any Court.
legal_principles.held: This court holds that these powers are to be exercised to quash criminal proceedings or complaints, as the case may be, and these powers can be exercised to secure the ends of justice or to prevent abuse of process of any Court.
cited_cases: Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab and others, (2012) 10 SCC 303
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — to prevent abuse of process

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party seeking quashing of criminal proceedings or complaints to demonstrate that the continuation of such proceedings would cause an abuse of process.
legal_principles.held: Burden lies on the party seeking quashing of criminal proceedings or complaints to demonstrate that the continuation of such proceedings would cause an abuse of process.
cited_cases: Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab and others, (2012) 10 SCC 303
legal_principles.significance: MEDIUM — to prevent abuse of process

outcome.final_order: Quashing of FIR No. 160 of 2023 and further proceedings pending before the Court of learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Sarkaghat, District Mandi, H.P.
